openQuestions.text: Does a repo-local overlay for hard-rules.json exist or is the vendored sidecar the only source?
Is there a uniform read-only probe for per-runtime adapter registration (Claude PreToolUse, opencode plugin, pi extension)?
How should repos without specs/ satisfy trailers.spec mustExist?

resolvedQuestions.text: What does the sk-code adaptation guide and `/doctor:sk-code setup` check, and how do those responsibilities divide?
Which sk-git policy inputs are repository-customizable, where are they set, and what behavior depends on them?
How do worktree naming/provisioning, Commit-Id allocation, hook trust, global hooks, and preflight advice interact?
What can a read-only sk-git setup check prove, and how does `/doctor:git` currently route and report?
Should setup be a new `/doctor:git` action or a separate command, and which proposals should be rejected?

keyFindings.text: `/doctor:sk-code` is a thin router, not an implementation: `sk-code.md` binds the route whose `command` is `/doctor:sk-code` out of `_routes.yaml`, loads the route's workflow YAML plus the presentation contract, and forbids agent dispatch or YAML edits from the Markdown. Its only target is `setup` (default when no positional is given); the only accepted flag is `--prompt=<text>`; anything else fails before YAML load. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/sk-code.md:10-36]

`/doctor:sk-code` is a thin router with one default target, `setup`; its command doc routes presentation and workflow assets while the YAML owns execution behavior. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/sk-code.md:8-16,29-50]

`/doctor:git` already exists with two `mutating: mutates` targets — `hooks` (dry-run plan over `git config speckit.hooks.<key>` then `--apply` after approval) and `standards` (status/init/set/disable/check over a `.sk-git/` contract dir named by `git config skgit.contractDir`, plus `validate-message.mjs --explain`). sk-git already has a doctor surface AND a per-repo override mechanism; a read-only setup target would be the route family's third member, not a new command family. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:236-274]

The route manifest `_routes.yaml` is the canonical routing and mutation-class manifest. Each route carries `command`, `target`, `yaml`, `setup_vars`, `allowed_flags`, `mutating` (`read-only | add-only | mutates`), `gate3_location`, `mcp_tools`, `script_invocations`, `trigger_phrases`. The sk-code route is `mutating: read-only` with `gate3_location: "n/a (read-only setup battery … writes nothing)"`. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:23-37,220-234]

The setup workflow is explicitly read-only: it forbids all write targets and requires repair commands to be reported for the operator to run. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-sk-code-setup.yaml:12-28,46-52]

The eight-leg battery checks provisioning, parent structure, metadata, route guard and sync, drift, derived freshness, and a parsed route decision; it reports PASS/FAIL/SKIP and repair text without applying repairs. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-sk-code-setup.yaml:48-52; .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/sk-code-setup-check.cjs:97-149,252-310]

The workflow `doctor-sk-code-setup.yaml` is single-step and hard-pinned read-only: `mutation_boundaries.read_only: true`, `allowed_targets: []`, `forbidden_targets: ["**/*"]`, with the invariant that every leg runs check-only and "Repair is an explicit operator action, never a side effect of a diagnostic." Exit code maps 0→STATUS=OK, 1→STATUS=FAIL, 2→STATUS=ERROR. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-sk-code-setup.yaml:23-28,46-60]

The adaptation guide and diagnostic have separate jobs: the README block tells users how to add or remove surfaces and what to keep, while `/doctor:sk-code setup` checks the resulting tree and names repairs. [SOURCE: specs/sk-code/011-sk-code-poinytail-based-refinement/026-external-surface-priority-build/005-external-user-guide/spec.md:71-79; .skilled/skills/sk-code/README.md:116-122; specs/sk-code/011-sk-code-poinytail-based-refinement/029-surface-setup-build/002-doctor-sk-code-setup/spec.md:36-50]

The battery `sk-code-setup-check.cjs` is a self-contained node script with four parts: a `LEGS` array (each leg = `{id, command(), run()}` spawning a child check from the repo root), a `JUDGES` map (leg result → `{ok, details[], repairs[]}`), a `report()` that prints `PASS|FAIL|SKIP <leg> <command>` lines plus indented `repair:` lines under failures and a final `STATUS=OK legs=8` / `STATUS=FAIL failed=<n> skipped=<n>`, and `main()` returning exit 0/1/2. `SK_CODE_SETUP_ROOT` overrides the repo root so the battery can be pointed at a fixture tree. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/sk-code-setup-check.cjs:39-41,83-149,155-311,331-369]

The eight legs are: `provisioning` (in-process `require.resolve('@spec-kit/shared/frontmatter/parse-frontmatter.js')`, no child), `parent-skill` (`parent-skill-check.cjs .skilled/skills/sk-code`), `root-metadata` (`ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs`), `guard` (`compiled-route-guard.cjs --json`), `sync` (`compiled-route-sync.cjs --check`), `drift-guards` (`run-all-drift-guards.sh`), `derived-freshness` (`ci-skill-derived-freshness.cjs --format json`), and `probe` (`compiled-route.cjs --hub sk-code --prompt <text>` must parse a final JSON line with `action:"route"` — the legacy stub exits 0 too, so exit code alone proves nothing). [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/sk-code-setup-check.cjs:97-148,252-280; .skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-sk-code-setup.yaml:49]

The battery is dependency-aware, not fail-fast: `PROVISION_DEPENDENTS = {parent-skill, root-metadata}` report SKIP (not FAIL) when provisioning fails, and a missing `.skilled/skills/sk-code/SKILL.md` reports provisioning FAIL with a "predates the v4 layout" repair while every other leg reports `SKIP … needs the v4 layout`. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/sk-code-setup-check.cjs:69,339-361]

Every FAIL leg prints the exact command that repairs it rather than fixing anything: provisioning→`bash .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-naming.sh provision .`, sync→`node .skilled/bin/compiled-route-sync.cjs`, derived-freshness→per-root `regenerate-skill-derived.cjs --root <name> --write`, probe-legacy→the guard's own `staleFix(hub)` text. Repairs are data in `JUDGES`, not actions. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/sk-code-setup-check.cjs:64,183-185,198-280]

The sk-code adaptation guide is the README block "What Adapting `sk-code` Looks Like": four before-you-start steps (provision, `git config --local skilled.trustRepoHooks true`, `bash .skilled/scripts/install-git-hooks.sh`, keep the authored routing source + `.opencode/skills` link), a 9-step remove-an-example recipe, a 5-step add-your-own-surface recipe (`/create:skill-parent update --surfaces <name>` + hand edits + canary fixture), and a Verify block listing the same six commands the battery wraps plus `/doctor:sk-code setup` itself. [SOURCE: README.md:1447-1489]

The sk-code battery's own provisioning repair is an sk-git script (`worktree-naming.sh provision .`), and its trust step is `skilled.trustRepoHooks` — the setup-check concept already crosses the sk-code/sk-git boundary, so an sk-git battery has precedent for checking shared infrastructure owned partly by other surfaces. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/sk-code-setup-check.cjs:64; README.md:1453-1454]

The placement decision is documented explicitly: "a new doctor command, `/doctor:sk-code`, with one read-only target, `setup`" — chosen because the family grammar is `/doctor:<owner> <target>` and the one-per-owner rule wants the sk-code hub as owner. A `sk-code-setup` hub mode was rejected because `packetKind` is only `workflow` or `surface` (setup is neither), no setup prompt would ever route to it, and it would cost 15+ files plus a contract change. [SOURCE: specs/sk-code/011-sk-code-poinytail-based-refinement/028-surface-setup-hardening-research/research/research.md:97-111,135]

Users may adapt the agent-facing git policy in `.skilled/skills/sk-git/SKILL.md`; today it requires fresh permission for pushes outside the allowlist and says the preflight hook advises while Git hooks enforce, so changing the prose without matching hook policy can leave agent guidance and enforcement out of sync; a doctor check can prove the skill file and referenced policy assets exist, but not that prose intent matches runtime behavior. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/SKILL.md:230-248,308-318]

The rejection catalogue is a checklist of tempting-but-wrong ideas: X1 hub mode (contract mismatch + cost); X2 target under `/doctor:skill-advisor` (wrong owner, undiscoverable name); X3 extending the `parent-skill` route (its contract is a structural audit — routing/drift failures would corrupt what a pass means); X4 mutating repairs inside the doctor (a read-only route may not write; `route-validate.sh` enforces it); X6 terminal add/remove script (the registry scrub and ROUTER.md edits need judgment; a second mutation path serves one caller class); X7 minting manifests inside `update --surfaces`; X11 advisor surface-awareness (no failure exists). [SOURCE: specs/sk-code/011-sk-code-poinytail-based-refinement/028-surface-setup-hardening-research/research/research.md:131-145]

Users may tune risky-command advisories in the adjacent `hard-rules.json`; it currently carries 17 warning rules, and a missing, malformed, or non-array file makes the reader return no rules while an unknown check is skipped, so those warnings disappear; the file is selected beside the loaded `SKILL.md` rather than through a separate repository setting, and a doctor check should prove valid JSON, unique rule IDs, recognized checks, and valid severities. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/hard-rules.json:1-104; .skilled/hooks/dispatch/lib/dispatch-rule-checks.mjs:12-23,259-282; .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/hooks/README.md:28-35]

A repository can change commit, PR, and branch contracts by copying the templates into `.sk-git/` or setting `skgit.contractDir`; the loader prefers that setting, then `.sk-git/`, then the repository's bundled assets, while a missing rules block means no enforcement and a malformed block blocks the gate, so setup should report the effective directory and each contract's enforced/not-enforced state rather than infer success from exit 0. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/SKILL.md:310-318; .skilled/skills/sk-git/assets/commit-message-template.md:177-184; .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/lib/message-contract.mjs:278-323; .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/validate-message.mjs:125-136,192-197]

The battery's leg list is not arbitrary — it is the executable form of the README guide's Verify block: the six documented verify commands, plus a provisioning precheck (the missing step a fresh clone needs) and the derived-metadata freshness gate (CI ran it but the user's battery did not), plus a probe that must parse `action:"route"` because the last README leg exited 0 on the legacy stub. [SOURCE: specs/sk-code/011-sk-code-poinytail-based-refinement/028-surface-setup-hardening-research/research/research.md:88-93,105,123; specs/sk-code/011-sk-code-poinytail-based-refinement/029-surface-setup-build/002-doctor-sk-code-setup/spec.md:35-44]

A repository can add branch globs to `scripts/remote-branch-allowlist.txt`; `main` and `skilled/v*` remain built in, and deleting or emptying the additive file only narrows exceptions, while a broad glob permits any session to publish matching updates; setup should identify the file actually resolved for this checkout and report representative allow/deny matches without pushing. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/remote-branch-allowlist.txt:1-9; .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-naming.sh:142-182; .skilled/skills/sk-git/references/remote-branch-policy.md:34-44]

The motivating failures define what a setup check is FOR: the guard printed `Re-mint: sk-code` with no command (F5), the route probe could not fail (F7), a CI gate was missing from the user battery (F16), and a fresh clone could not reach green following the guide (F1-F3). A doctor setup exists to make invisible/unactionable failures visible with named repairs. [SOURCE: specs/sk-code/011-sk-code-poinytail-based-refinement/028-surface-setup-hardening-research/research/research.md:85-113]

Phase ordering was deliberate: P1 (029/001) fixed the hand-followed path first — README before-you-start lines, guard stale-manifest message naming its commands, named failure instead of a stack — and only then P2 (029/002) built the battery that prints those same repair texts. The battery depends on P1 because it prints P1's repair strings. Lesson: the documented journey must be self-sufficient before a battery is worth running. [SOURCE: specs/sk-code/011-sk-code-poinytail-based-refinement/029-surface-setup-build/spec.md:85-118; specs/sk-code/011-sk-code-poinytail-based-refinement/028-surface-setup-hardening-research/research/research.md:149-174]

Naming was weighed: `setup` was chosen over `surfaces` because the battery also covers provisioning — the target name must cover the whole check surface, not just the resource being adapted. [SOURCE: specs/sk-code/011-sk-code-poinytail-based-refinement/028-surface-setup-hardening-research/research/research.md:111]

Route additions have a fixed recipe and a validator: append a row to `_routes.yaml`, list it in the command's router and presentation, run `route-validate.sh`; every script the route runs is enumerated in `script_invocations`. The acceptance gate for the new route was `route-validate.sh` exit 0 plus pristine/stale/unprovisioned copy runs (S-1..S-3 ledger rows). [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:36-38; specs/sk-code/011-sk-code-poinytail-based-refinement/029-surface-setup-build/002-doctor-sk-code-setup/spec.md:80-95]

The 026 packet already shipped the "external surface" semantics this research builds on: a user-added surface is scaffolded ahead of the native `sk-code-opencode` in `tieBreak` so it wins keyword ties (doctor check 5l fails a surface placed after it), OpenCode is marked native (keep), Webflow/Obsidian are optional examples (removable via the 9-step recipe). [SOURCE: specs/sk-code/011-sk-code-poinytail-based-refinement/026-external-surface-priority-build/005-external-user-guide/spec.md:60-83; README.md:1449,1472]

Battery cost and growth were considered acceptable: ~15 s measured (E6), one pass per leg, and the drift-guards leg is the one that grows — a sk-git battery should likewise time-budget its legs. [SOURCE: specs/sk-code/011-sk-code-poinytail-based-refinement/029-surface-setup-build/002-doctor-sk-code-setup/spec.md:118]

A repository can relocate numbered worktrees with environment variable `SPECKIT_WORKTREE_BASE` or Git config `speckit.worktreeBase`; the environment wins, then local or inherited Git config, then `<main-worktree>/.worktrees`, and relative paths resolve against the main checkout, so a setup check should report the effective resolved base and compare it with existing worktree paths. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-naming.sh:11-17,58-77]

`SKILL.md` is prose AND contract: its rules are behavior (ask-first workspace rule; NEVER create branches directly; remote-push permission; commit grammar `worktrees/NNN-slug` / `branches/NNN-slug`), while the mechanical pieces defer to files a repository can override — the rules block in `assets/commit-message-template.md` §7, `scripts/remote-branch-allowlist.txt`, `worktree-naming.sh`, `worktree-provision-paths.txt`, `hard-rules.json`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/SKILL.md:205-258,285-318]

The `Spec:` trailer and `attribution.forbidden` are repo-shaped assumptions inside the shipped rules block: `trailers.spec` pins `root: "specs"`, `forbiddenPrefix: "specs/"`, `mustExist: true` — a repo without `specs/` packets must override or disable that rule via its own `.sk-git/` copy; `attribution.forbiddenKeys: [Co-Authored-By, Claude-Session]` + `forbiddenTrailerValuePattern: "anthropic"` may be wrong for repos that want attribution. These are exactly the `git-standards.cjs set`/`disable` levers. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/assets/commit-message-template.md:257-269]

The commit message contract is data, not prose: the ```json "Enforced rules" block in `commit-message-template.md` §7 (kind/version/help/passthroughSubjects/subject/body/trailers/attribution/breakingFooterPattern) is read by `validate-message.mjs` and enforced identically by the commit-msg hook, pre-push hook, agent gate and CI. The template says so explicitly: "Another repository gets its own rules by carrying its own copy of this template, in `.sk-git/` at its root or in the directory git config `skgit.contractDir` names." [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/assets/commit-message-template.md:177-184,216-271]

The repository-owned `scripts/worktree-provision-paths.txt` lists package directories and optional build outputs; `create` makes a numbered branch and worktree and provisions by default, while `--no-provision` opts out, so a read-only check can prove the list exists, its package paths resolve, and declared outputs are present, but it cannot prove that a future install or build will succeed without running them. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-naming.sh:398-425,508-559; .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-provision-paths.txt:1-28]

Contract-dir resolution order is `skgit.contractDir` (git config, file scope only — a command-scoped `-c`/`GIT_CONFIG_*` value is deliberately ignored so no invocation can switch rules off) → `.sk-git/` at repo root → shipped `assets/` under `.skilled/` or `.opencode/`. A `skgit.contractDir` pointing at a missing directory throws `ContractError`, and `validate-message.mjs` exit 2 is treated as a block — so a stale contractDir breaks EVERY commit, the highest-blast-radius misconfiguration in this surface. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/lib/message-contract.mjs:278-307,314-324; .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/validate-message.mjs:17-18,222]

Local `git config skilled.commitId true|false` overrides Commit-Id autodetection; without it, the shared policy opts repositories in when their checkout ships the allocator/toolchain sentinel or recent history has a valid trailer, so changing it to `false` stops stamping and the required-trailer check even when the toolchain is present, while the shipped author template still describes Commit-Id as mandatory. [SOURCE: .skilled/scripts/git-hooks/lib/commit-id-policy.sh:17-40; .skilled/scripts/git-hooks/prepare-commit-msg:103-119,286-313; .skilled/scripts/git-hooks/commit-msg:69-75; .skilled/skills/sk-git/assets/commit-message-template.md:41-47]

Commit-Id ordinals are seven digits, shared across linked worktrees through a lock and high-water mark in the common Git directory, never back-filled; the stamper leaves a message unstamped if its policy helper or allocator is missing or allocation fails, and `commit-msg` blocks a required ID that is absent, so setup should distinguish allocator presence, policy result, and actual hook installation rather than equate a configured opt-in with working enforcement. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/commit-id-naming.sh:5-18,30-48,190-231; .skilled/scripts/git-hooks/prepare-commit-msg:97-119,303-313; .skilled/scripts/git-hooks/commit-msg:60-76]

`git-standards.cjs` (the `/doctor:git standards` backend) already is the per-repo override tool for commit/PR/branch rules: `status` reports resolved dir + source + editable + per-kind enforced/broken/drift; `init` copies the three shipped templates into `.sk-git/` (dry-run default, never overwrites, warns when contractDir outranks `.sk-git/`); `set <kind> <dotted.path> <json>` refuses to write shipped assets and refuses a change that breaks `contractShapeErrors`; `disable <kind>` removes the Enforced-rules section so that kind is unenforced; `check` exits 0/1/2 on clean/drift/broken. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/git-standards.cjs:7-37,158-189,217-351]

`hard-rules.json` is 17 warn-severity advisory rules `{id, check, message}` evaluated by the shared preflight advisory hook against live repository state — firing on the risky state, never bare verbs; advise-only, never blocks; suppression is `SKGIT_ADVISORY=0` (global) or `SKGIT_ADVISORY_SKIP=<rule-id>`/prefix. What a user would change: rule texts, severities, or add repo-specific rules; what breaks: a malformed JSON or a rule the engine's `check` key doesn't implement silently weakens the advisory without failing anything. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/hard-rules.json:1-104; .skilled/skills/sk-git/SKILL.md:243-257]

The remote-branch allowlist is `main` + `skilled/v*` (hardcoded, checked before the file is read) + globs in `scripts/remote-branch-allowlist.txt`. The file can only narrow, never widen — "an operator-editable file must fail toward MORE asking." Creation of a remote branch always needs `SPECKIT_ALLOW_REMOTE_PUSH=<branch>`; `=1` only permits updates to existing remote branches, set per-invocation never per-session. The pre-push hook backstops; the concern fails open if `worktree-naming.sh` is missing/unsourceable. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/references/remote-branch-policy.md:30-56,78-104; .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/remote-branch-allowlist.txt:1-9]

Worktree naming/provisioning is a shipped script with per-repo knobs: branch grammar `worktrees/NNN-slug` and `branches/NNN-slug` (independent 001-999 sequences, locked counter in the common git dir seeded from high-water + all matching refs + registered worktrees, never reissued); reserved lanes `skilled/v*`, `backup/`, `main`, and the launch-wrapper lane `work/<runtime>/<slug>`; the worktree BASE relocates via `SPECKIT_WORKTREE_BASE` env > `git config speckit.worktreeBase` > `.worktrees`. Provisioning installs the per-repo dependency list in `worktree-provision-paths.txt` (dir per line, optional `npm run build` artifact check) under the invariant that no shared path may resolve a repo-internal reference back to the source checkout. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-naming.sh:5-77; .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-provision-paths.txt:1-40; .skilled/skills/sk-git/SKILL.md:292,296]

The Commit-Id allocator is `commit-id-naming.sh`: 7-digit ordinals (`0000001`-`9999999`, `0000000` invalid) minted in commit order under a common-git-dir lock, cold-start rescanning `git log --all` for the max, high-water file as cache, never reissued. The `prepare-commit-msg` hook stamps `Commit-Id:` (and `Spec:` only when the trailer belongs), with amend/cherry-pick/rebase semantics documented. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/commit-id-naming.sh:1-75; .skilled/scripts/git-hooks/prepare-commit-msg:6-8,97-111,370]

Commit-Id is opt-in per repository via `skilled.commitId`: `cip_repo_wants_ids` reads `git config --local --bool skilled.commitId` FIRST (true=on, false=off), and only local config counts so a cloned repo cannot switch itself in or out. Absent the flag it auto-detects: repo shipping `.skilled/` or `.opencode/` sk-git allocator or the system-spec-kit sentinel, or ≥1 `Commit-Id` trailer in the last 50 commits. [SOURCE: .skilled/scripts/git-hooks/lib/commit-id-policy.sh:19-45]

A clone's own hook scripts run only when its Git common directory matches the installed hook checkout or local config sets `skilled.trustRepoHooks=true`; command-line and environment config do not grant trust, and trust applies to every branch in that checkout and its worktrees, so a setup check should show the local trust value and explain which repository code it authorizes. [SOURCE: .skilled/scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit:28-57]

The global hooks are shipped sources under `.skilled/scripts/git-hooks/` symlinked into `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` by `.skilled/scripts/install-git-hooks.sh` — honoring repo-local or global `core.hooksPath` automatically, and usually installed machine-wide. `--status` prints the hooksPath scope, per-hook resolved target, a `SHADOWED` warning when the installed link resolves outside the checkout, and the resolved message contract (`validate-message.mjs --repo --explain`). [SOURCE: .skilled/scripts/install-git-hooks.sh:107-144; .skilled/scripts/git-hooks/README.md:15-18]

`/doctor:git` is already a thin router in exactly the sk-code shape: target + setup values resolved from `_routes.yaml`, presentation contract loaded, workflow YAML executed from `.skilled/commands/doctor/assets/` — so a `setup` target is one route row + one workflow YAML + one read-only check script, and the existing `hooks`/`standards` targets already own mutation (`git-hook-gates.cjs`, `git-standards.cjs`), which a setup check would read-only invoke (`status`/`list`) rather than duplicate. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/git.md:3-10,22-67]

Install safety is already solved and a setup check should verify rather than redo it: the installer refuses to overwrite a foreign hook (a symlink counts as ours only if it resolves under `.skilled/` or `.opencode/` `scripts/git-hooks`), warns-and-skips, and `--uninstall` removes only own symlinks — coexistence with husky/pre-commit/lefthook is the designed posture, and installing from a linked worktree prints a dangling-symlink warning. [SOURCE: .skilled/scripts/install-git-hooks.sh:72-105,146-177,188-197]

`.skilled/scripts/git-hooks/` is the lifecycle-hook source, while Git resolves installed hooks through the effective `core.hooksPath`; installer `--status` reports the configured scope, resolved target directory, each hook's link/source and shadowing, plus the effective message contract, so a read-only setup path can reuse that status data without reinstalling anything. [SOURCE: .skilled/scripts/install-git-hooks.sh:29-50,96-149; .skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-git-hooks.yaml:78-83]

Persistent optional gate switches live in local or global `speckit.hooks.<key>` config and the `gates.tsv` registry; `/doctor:git hooks` can change those gates, but intentionally refuses saved per-push approvals, leaves commit-message rules to its `standards` target, and sends whole-hook kill switches to `/doctor:env`, while `core.hooksPath` is outside its mutation boundary. [SOURCE: .skilled/scripts/git-hooks/lib/gate-config.sh:5-16,20-39; .skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-git-hooks.yaml:22-42,63-72; .skilled/commands/doctor/git.md:51-67]

`skilled.trustRepoHooks` is the repo-side opt-in that decides whether the globally installed hooks run *this* repository's own gate scripts: an identical block in all six lifecycle hooks keeps the selected source root only when the target shares the hooks' checkout (or a worktree of it) or sets `git config --local skilled.trustRepoHooks true`; a `-c` flag or `GIT_CONFIG_*` never counts, local config is never cloned, and trust covers the repository not a branch. Untrusted → `SOURCE_ROOT=/dev/null/.skilled-untrusted` → treated as a repo without the toolchain, with a NOTICE naming the enable command. [SOURCE: .skilled/scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit:28-56; .skilled/scripts/git-hooks/README.md:34-36]

`commit-msg` deliberately sits outside the trust block: it finds `validate-message.mjs` beside the installed hook and enforces *the target repository's own* rules block even in untrusted clones; it has no bypass and `--no-verify` only defers the check to `pre-push` and CI. So the message contract is the one enforcement a repo cannot escape by staying untrusted. [SOURCE: .skilled/scripts/git-hooks/README.md:34-36]
